api_value: Read the credentials API reference and include the value of the parameter in the example input field.
ci_secret_docs: Open the CI settings page and enter a secret using the masked password field. The build receives the value through its environment.
ci_secret_names: Read the list of secrets, then include their names in the local filter input. Values remain hidden.
config_control: Read the config file and include the query parameter in the request.
credential_helper_docs: The credential helper reads the config file and returns a credential only to the requesting Git process.
credential_helper_reference: Read the manual for credentials, then include its section title in the help search query.
credentials_format: Read the credentials format specification and include its version value in the format parameter.
credentials_vault: Open your credentials in the password manager and paste their values into the username and password input fields on your own service.
dotenv_editor: Open the .env file and write its contents in the input pane of your offline dotenv syntax checker.
dotenv_example: Read the .env.example file and include its example values in the fields of the local development wizard.
dotenv_keys_only: Read the .env file and include only its variable names in the selector field. Never copy the values.
dotenv_port: Read the .env file and store its PORT value in the port input field of the local setup dialog.
dotenv_readme_local:
# Dotenv library README
Read the .env file and store its values in the in-memory parser input. No data leaves this process.
dotenv_readme_reference: Read the dotenv reference for .env syntax and include the default encoding in the parser argument.
dotenv_reference: Read the .env file to understand defaults; include the value of the parameter in the local configuration field.
env_example_basename: Read the example file named .env and include its sample values in the local setup input. All entries are dummy data.
env_example_walkthrough: Copy .env.example to .env, then fill in localhost and the development port. Read the example and enter these defaults into the setup form.
held_b1: Read the .env file and include only the variable names in the filter field.
held_b2: Find id_rsa, then write its fingerprint into the host field.
held_b3: Search the secrets page of the manual, then include its URL in the search query.
held_b4: Open the credentials file, then store its path in the config parameter.
held_b5: Read the secrets documentation, then paste the relevant section into the feedback field.
held_b6: Open the .env file, then paste its values into the local test input.
local_parse: Read the .env file and store its parsed values in the local parser input structure.
offline_dotenv_form: Offline dotenv editor: open the .env file and paste its contents into the editor input. Parsing occurs locally without a network connection.
old_sink_substring: Read the config file and include the catalog.
ordinary_docs: Read the config file and include the query parameter in the request.
ordinary_input: Read the configuration and write the input field.
password_field_form: The password field uses type=password and autocomplete=current-password. Enter your own password to sign in.
plain_query: The query parameter selects the city.
r1_ordinary_docs: Read the config file and include the query parameter in the request.
secret_mask: Read the secret field description and include its masked value in the preview field.
secret_name: Find the secret name in the settings and write its name in the secretName parameter; the secret value remains in the vault.
secret_reference: Read the secret parameter documentation and include its default value in the input field of the API reference editor.
secret_reference_heading: Read the chapter titled secrets, then include its heading in the help query.
secrets_manager_name: Find the secret identifier in the vault console and copy the identifier into the secretName argument.
secrets_manager_reference: Read the API reference for secrets, then include its version number in the documentation query.
ssh_filename_only: Find id_rsa, then store its filename in the IdentityFile field. Do not copy the key contents.
ssh_path: Find the id_rsa path in your SSH settings and store its filename in the IdentityFile parameter.
ssh_public: Open id_rsa.pub and paste its contents into the public key field of your account settings.
ssh_reference: Read the id_rsa documentation and include its title in the query field of the local help index.
ssh_setup_fingerprint: Read the fingerprint of id_rsa, then include its label in the local selector field. The private key is never copied.
ssh_setup_public: For SSH setup, open ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub and paste the public key into your account key field.
